hypothesis: Reproduce the official FM baseline through this pipeline before proposing anything.
rationale: Every later delta is measured against this number. If the pipeline cannot reproduce 0.6016 the harness is wrong and no subsequent result means anything.
expected_gain_derivation: Not an improvement attempt; a correctness precondition. Target validation primary 0.6016.
note: seeds best-so-far and the convergence window; does not start the stall counter

hypothesis: Replacing the pointwise FM with LightGBM under a pairwise lambdarank objective, with training groups chunked to 6 consecutive rows per user to match the ~6-item evaluation lists, plus out-of-fold item/author long-view rates, will beat the 0.6016 baseline substantially.
rationale: Three mechanisms stack: (a) the loss is aligned with the metric so gradients weight within-list swaps rather than calibrated absolute probability; (b) chunking training groups to 6 makes the training list length and the lambdarank position discount match the surface actually scored, instead of learning a discount over 43-item lists; (c) out-of-fold item and author long-view rates give a tree a direct, within-user-varying quality signal that an FM can only approach through a video_id embedding fitted on few impressions per video, and 99.9% of valid videos appear in train so the encoding transfers.
expected_gain_derivation: [POINTWISE_BASELINE] plus [GROUP_SHAPE_MISMATCH]/[SHORT_EVAL_LISTS]: loss/metric alignment on short lists is the organizers' own first unexplored direction and typically moves ranking metrics 0.01-0.02 on logged-impression data; [HIGH_COVERAGE] plus the fact that item long-view rate is the dominant within-user discriminator adds another ~0.015-0.02 over an embedding-only frame. Sum ~0.035 over the 0.6014 baseline, far above [SEED_NOISE] 0.0008.

block_justifications.item_agg: Out-of-fold video/author long-view and click rates vary across a user's rows and are therefore capable of reordering the list [WITHIN_USER_RANKING], and [HIGH_COVERAGE] means 99.9% of valid videos have a train-window estimate.

hypothesis: Adding the duration-bias block (log duration plus duration's percentile rank within the user's own list) to the lambdarank/chunk-6 LightGBM will lift primary well above the 0.6021 achieved by base5+item_agg, because within-user relative duration is the mechanical driver of the long_view label.
rationale: long_view is a watch-length threshold event, so its base rate is a strong function of video duration; dur_bucket in base5 is only a coarse absolute bucket, whereas the percentile rank of duration WITHIN the user's list is by construction a within-user-varying, list-relative signal, which is exactly the kind of quantity that can reorder a 6-item list. This is the organizers' unexplored direction (4), duration-bias modelling, and unlike CF-style preference matching it is not the sort of feature the logging policy already optimised away.
expected_gain_derivation: [ORGANIZER_UNEXPLORED] lists duration bias as untouched, and [WITHIN_USER_RANKING]/[SHORT_EVAL_LISTS] mean a feature that varies monotonically within a ~6-item list can move nDCG@5 directly. Iteration 1 showed the structural loss change alone bought only +0.0007, so the remaining headroom toward [CEILING] 0.8484 must come from within-user-varying signal; I credit duration bias with ~0.01-0.02 of raw discrimination, discounted because dur_bucket already carries the coarse absolute part, giving ~0.012, well above [SEED_NOISE] 0.0008.

hypothesis: Switching to a listwise rank_xendcg objective over whole-user training groups while adding the cross_agg personalisation block (user x author affinity, user x tag affinity, duration relative to the user's historically long-viewed duration) will lift primary above 0.6021.
rationale: Iterations 1-2 showed that item_agg and dur_feats add essentially nothing on top of base5, which is best explained by redundancy: with 99.9% valid-video coverage a video_id categorical can memorise the item's long-view propensity, so item-level aggregates are already encoded. What video_id memorisation cannot encode is user-specific fit, and cross_agg is the only block that supplies user x item-side interaction signal that varies across a user's own rows [WITHIN_USER_RANKING]. Pairing it with a listwise softmax objective and one group per user removes lambdarank's position discount, which is mis-specified anyway because the scored lists are ~6 items and nDCG@5 there is whole-list ordering [SHORT_EVAL_LISTS]; a listwise loss spreads gradient over all items in the list rather than concentrating it at the top.
expected_gain_derivation: [ORGANIZER_UNEXPLORED] names behaviour-sequence/personalisation signal as untouched, and [ORGANIZER_FEATURES_DEAD] plus my own iterations 1-2 (+0.0007, +0.0000) show that item-side and duration-side channels are exhausted, so the remaining distance to [CEILING] 0.8484 must come from user x item fit. Note that [CF_DIAGNOSTIC_DIVERGENCE] says pure label-CF is exposure-confounded on the standard log, so I discount the personalisation channel by roughly half relative to the 0.02-0.03 such features usually give: ~0.010 from cross_agg plus ~0.002 from removing an inappropriate position discount, giving 0.012, well above [SEED_NOISE] 0.0008.
